name: South Korea

demographics.notes: World's lowest total fertility rate creates significant structural pressure on military conscription pools and future labor supply.

economy.notes: Asia's 4th largest and world's 13th largest economy; advanced industrial nation leading in semiconductors, electric vehicle batteries, shipbuilding, consumer electronics, and automotive manufacturing.
major_exports: Liquid crystal and OLED display panels
Commercial cargo vessels and LNG carriers
major_imports: Refined battery chemicals and critical rare earths

military.defence_spending_pct_gdp_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS), 2024 data, extracted from user-provided dataset (file last updated 2026-02-24)
military.arms_exports_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPRT.KD), constant USD, from user-provided dataset
key_equipment_or_doctrines: Three-Axis Defence System: Kill Chain pre-emption, Korea Air & Missile Defence (KAMD), Korea Massive Punishment and Retaliation (KMPR)
K2 Black Panther Main Battle Tank & K9 Thunder 155mm Self-Propelled Howitzer (major export successes to Poland, Australia, Egypt, Romania)
KF-21 Boramae 4.5+ generation indigenous multirole fighter & FA-50 light combat aircraft
Dosan Ahn Changho-class diesel-electric attack submarines equipped with Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missiles (SLBMs)
US Forces Korea (USFK): ~28,500 active US personnel stationed at Camp Humphreys and Osan Air Base

primary_sources: Crude oil (38% of total primary energy)
Nuclear power (16% of primary energy, ~30% of electric power)
energy.note: Virtually 100% dependent on imported fossil fuels transiting maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz and Malacca); counterbalanced by an expanding commercial nuclear fleet (APR-1400 reactors).

major_ports: Port of Busan (World's 6th busiest container transshipment hub, primary maritime lifeline)
Port of Incheon (Yellow Sea gateway to capital area and China)
Port of Gwangyang (Deepwater steel and container terminal)
Port of Ulsan (Major petrochemical and energy terminal)
strategic_airports: Incheon International Airport (ICN, premier East Asian passenger and cargo hub)
Gimpo International Airport (GMP, regional metropolitan hub)
Gimhae International Airport (PUS, southeastern logistics gateway)
infrastructure.energy_grid_resilience: Isolated national electrical grid operating as an 'energy island' with no cross-border interconnection due to North Korean isolation; high domestic transmission reliability.
infrastructure.digital_infrastructure: World-leading fiber-to-the-home and 5G penetration; Gyeonggi Mega Semiconductor Cluster at Yongin and Pyeongtaek; primary subsea fiber cable landings at Busan, Geoje, and Taean.

top_partners: China (largest bilateral trading partner, critical market for intermediate semiconductor components)
United States (crucial export market for vehicles, technology, and security equipment)
Vietnam (primary overseas manufacturing base for Korean electronics)
Japan (vital source of specialty chemicals and precision precision engineering)
Australia (primary supplier of iron ore, lithium, and LNG)
chokepoint_exposure: Strait of Malacca (over 80% of imported crude oil and maritime trade with Europe and Middle East)
Taiwan Strait (critical shipping corridor for container exports to global markets)
Strait of Hormuz (over 70% of imported crude oil supplies originating in Gulf states)

core_competencies: Leading global producer of memory semiconductors (Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix control ~60% of DRAM and NAND markets)
Global leader in EV lithium-ion batteries and battery cell chemistries (LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, SK On)
World-class naval and commercial shipbuilding technology, leading in LNG carriers and ammonia-fueled vessels
High-density consumer electronics, OLED display manufacturing, and telecommunications equipment
tech_vulnerabilities: Heavy reliance on ASML (Netherlands) for Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) photolithography machinery
Dependence on Japanese specialty chemicals (photoresists, fluorinated polyimides, high-purity hydrogen fluoride)
Substantial dependence on China for processing and refining critical minerals (graphite, lithium, cobalt, nickel)

land_borders: North Korea (238 km along the Military Demarcation Line / DMZ)

politics.executive: President of the Republic of Korea serves as head of state and head of government with strong executive authority for a single 5-year term.
politics.legislature: Unicameral National Assembly (Gukhoe) comprising 300 members elected every 4 years.
politics.judiciary: Independent judicial system headed by the Supreme Court and the Constitutional Court.

nuclear.delivery_systems: Conventional ballistic and cruise missiles (Hyunmoo-IV and Hyunmoo-V high-yield bunker-busters, submarine-launched ballistic missiles on KSS-III class submarines).
nuclear.notes: Non-nuclear weapons state under the NPT. Operates 26 commercial nuclear reactors. Relies on the US extended nuclear umbrella codified under the 2023 Washington Declaration and bilateral Nuclear Consultative Group (NCG).

strategic_priorities: North Korea multi-domain deterrence and counter-artillery protection of the Greater Seoul Metropolitan Area
Strengthening the US-ROK Alliance and institutionalizing the trilateral security partnership with the United States and Japan (Camp David framework)
Securing semiconductor supply chains, lithography tool access, and mineral diversification away from single-source dependencies
Expanding defense industrial exports and defense diplomacy globally under the 'Global Pivotal State' (GPS) vision
Safeguarding unimpeded maritime transit through the Taiwan Strait, South China Sea, and Malacca Strait
dependencies: Near-total dependence on imported crude oil, LNG, and coal (93% net import dependence ratio) transiting maritime chokepoints
Critical mineral supply chains reliant on Chinese refining (graphite, lithium, rare earth magnets)
Advanced semiconductor tooling reliance on European (ASML EUV) and American EDA software ecosystems
Extended nuclear deterrence umbrella guaranteed by the United States
vulnerabilities: Extreme geographic exposure: Greater Seoul Metropolitan Area (26M people, 50% of national population) lies within 40-50 km of the DMZ, in direct range of ~1,000 North Korean hardened long-range artillery and rocket systems

Maritime chokepoint exposure: Over 85% of trade by sea passes through the Taiwan Strait and South China Sea; a blockade or conflict in the Taiwan Strait would immediately disrupt industrial energy and trade lines
Severe demographic decline: World's lowest fertility rate (0.72) imposes rapid structural reduction on mandatory military conscription intakes and future economic growth
Geopolitical crossfire between primary security guarantor (USA) and largest trading partner (China)
strengths: Global semiconductor anchor: Dominates over 60% of the world's memory chips (DRAM/NAND), making global electronics supply chains dependent on Korean fabrication stability
High-throughput, rapid-delivery defense industrial base capable of producing world-class tanks (K2), self-propelled artillery (K9), and combat aircraft (FA-50) faster than Western competitors
Advanced technological ecosystem spanning tier-1 shipbuilding, electric vehicle batteries, consumer electronics, and high-speed communications
High-readiness standing military of 500,000 personnel backed by an extensive 3.1 million trained reserve force and forward-stationed US Forces Korea (USFK)
